abstract: We study one explicit quartic-CM case of the Hodge conjecture for abelian varieties that lies beyond imaginary-quadratic Weil-class methods. Let $\alpha=(7,10,13,19,22,28)$ be a degree-$33$ Fermat fourfold character and $B_8$ the associated eight-dimensional ramified Prym factor of a cyclic-cover Jacobian. Unconditionally, using exact Frobenius computations at two primes, we show $\operatorname{End}^0_{\overline{\mathbf Q}}(B_8)=E=\mathbf Q(\zeta_{33})^{\langle 4\rangle}$ and $Hg(B_8)=\operatorname{Res}_{E^+/\mathbf Q}SU_E$ with $E^+=\mathbf Q(\sqrt{33})$. A structural theorem for balanced special-unitary abelian varieties then gives $\operatorname{Hdg}^2(B_8)_{\mathbf Q}=D^2(B_8)\oplus W_E(B_8)$, where $W_E(B_8)=\bigwedge_E^4H^1(B_8,\mathbf Q)$, and shows that the classical and generalized Hodge conjectures for every self-power $B_8^n$ are equivalent to algebraicity of $W_E(B_8)$. The source Fermat block is algebraic by Aoki's level-$66$ identity, and alternatively by a cubic-to-Fermat correspondence elaborating the cubic-scroll strategy of Favero–Kelly. Our main contribution is an explicit transfer: a common finite quotient of a Kummer curve product and the Fermat character quotient, a Poincaré curve-to-Prym divisor correspondence, and contraction along the small diagonal of $B_8$ give a single Chow correspondence carrying the source block onto $W_E(B_8)$, with exact normalization $5^{-3}$ relative to canonical Galois descent. This avoids the semiregularity step in secant-sheaf approaches. The main theorem is stated as a single chain: four explicit quotient hypotheses H1–H4 imply algebraicity of $W_E(B_8)$, which implies the rest; our arguments for H1–H4 are given separately. Under H1–H4, $W_E(B_8)$ is algebraic and the classical and generalized Hodge conjectures hold for all $B_8^n$. The exact computations are supplied. We do not claim the Hodge conjecture for $X_{33}^4$ or in general.
author: lihongmin
change_summary: Revision addressing the v1 review. (1) Restored the cube root: all instances of K_0(\sqrt[15]{5}) and \lambda with \sqrt[15]{5} now read \sqrt[3]{5}, matching the calculation and the computations (the [15] came from a citation-renumbering error). (2) Recorded the reduction choices \zeta_5 -> 64 mod 331 and \zeta_5 -> 247 mod 661; rewrote Reproducibility with the actual dependencies; supplement reduced to the 13 programs used, with a README. (3) Made the conditional status consistent: one dependency chain H1–H4 => W_E(B_8) algebraic => HC/GHC for all B_8^n, stated in the introduction, Proposition 2.1 (now explicitly 'Assume H1–H4'), Section 9, title and abstract; removed review-status wording from the theorem. (4) Attribution: the cubic construction is described as an elaboration of Favero–Kelly [24] with corrected cubic equation; the Jumagulov level-66 identity is credited; the OpenAI discussion is condensed and states that [7] with the CM-Hodge claim would also bear on W_E(B_8), the distinction being that we avoid that input. (5) Notation: replaced the corrupted superscript [17] by (4) in \bar q_*^{(4)}; renamed duplicate labels (second (1.0) -> (1.0b); Proposition 5.1 and Lemma 4.1 in Section 2 -> Proposition 2.2, Lemma 2.3; removed duplicate tag (6.12)); fixed reference numbering inside the bibliography (Markman entry). Wording made plainer throughout; no mathematical claims added.
title: A small-diagonal transfer from a degree-33 Fermat character to the quartic-CM determinant of a Prym eightfold, and the Hodge conjecture for its powers under explicit quotient hypotheses
